Identify TFs and classify them in families

Source: R/02_classification.R
classify_tfs.Rd

TFs are classified using the classification schemes of PlantTFDB, TAPscan, Plant-TFClass, CIS-BP, and TFClass (see list_schemes()).

Usage

classify_tfs(domain_annotation = NULL, scheme = "all", min_shared = 0.1)

Arguments

domain_annotation

A list of data frames with domain annotation, as returned by annotate_domains().

scheme

Character indicating which classification scheme(s) to return. Either 'all' (all schemes for which domain annotation is available) or one or more of 'PlantTFDB', 'TAPscan', 'PlantTFClass', 'CISBP', and 'TFClass'. Default: 'all'.

min_shared

Numeric indicating the minimum fraction of 5-mers shared with a reference TF to assign a C2H2 ZF TF to a single TFClass family (see details). Only used for TFClass. Default: 0.1.

Value

A data frame with one row per gene and the following variables (if scheme = "all"):

Gene

Gene ID.

PlantTFDB_family

TF family according to PlantTFDB.

PlantTFDB_subfamily

TF subfamily according to PlantTFDB.

TAPscan_family

TF family according to TAPscan.

TAPscan_subfamily

TF subfamily according to TAPscan.

TAP_class

Class of transcription-associated protein (TAP) according to TAPscan: transcription factor (TF), transcriptional regulator (TR), or putative TAP (PT). See data(tap_class).

PlantTFClass_superclass

TF superclass according to Plant-TFClass.

PlantTFClass_class

TF class according to Plant-TFClass.

PlantTFClass_family

TF family according to Plant-TFClass.

CISBP_family

TF family according to CIS-BP.

TFClass_superclass

TF superclass according to TFClass.

TFClass_class

TF class according to TFClass.

TFClass_family

TF family according to TFClass.

Only genes classified by at least one scheme are included. Genes not classified by a scheme have NA in the respective variables. Genes assigned to more than one PlantTFDB family have families (and subfamilies, in the same order) separated by ';'.

If only some schemes are used, only variable Gene and the variables of the chosen schemes are returned, and only genes classified by at least one of the chosen schemes are included. Note that TAPscan classifies not only TFs, but also transcriptional regulators and putative TAPs, which can be distinguished using the variable TAP_class.

Details

PlantTFDB and TAPscan classifications are based on the domains found in each gene. Plant-TFClass is a structure-based classification of TFs into superclasses, classes, and families, and Plant-TFClass classifications are inferred from TAPscan classifications using a correspondence table between the two classification systems. When a TAPscan subfamily corresponds to more than one Plant-TFClass family (e.g., TAPscan's AP2 includes Plant-TFClass's AP2, ERF/DREB, and RAV), PlantTFDB subfamilies are used to resolve the ambiguity. If the ambiguity cannot be resolved (e.g., the gene was not classified by PlantTFDB), all possible classifications are reported, separated by ';'.

CIS-BP classifications are based on the set of DNA-binding domains (DBDs) found in each gene. TFClass is a classification of TFs into superclasses, classes, families, and subfamilies based on the structure of their DBDs, and TFClass classifications are inferred from CIS-BP families using a correspondence table between the two classification systems. As TFClass includes only TFs of human and other mammals, it should be used only for mammals (use CIS-BP for other eukaryotes). TFs of CIS-BP families that do not occur in mammals (e.g., most plant and fungal TF families) are not classified by TFClass. CIS-BP families with multiple types of DBDs that are not in the correspondence table are classified based on each DBD's family; if these are in different TFClass classes or families, all possible superclasses, classes, and families are reported, separated by ';'.

Some CIS-BP families correspond to more than one TFClass family (e.g., CIS-BP's Homeodomain corresponds to TFClass families HOX, NK, TALE-type HD, and others). TFs in these families are assigned to a single TFClass family using reference TFs of human and mouse with known TFClass families, as follows:

  • C2H2 ZF: TFs are assigned to the family of the reference C2H2 ZF TF that shares the largest fraction of the TF's amino acid 5-mers (ignoring 5-mers found in > 2% of the reference TFs), if this fraction is >= min_shared.

  • Other families: TFs are scanned with profile HMMs built from the DNA-binding domains of the reference TFs in each TFClass family, and assigned to the family with the highest score, if this score is >= 10 bits higher than the score of any other possible family.

TFs that cannot be assigned to a single family (e.g., C2H2 ZF TFs that are specific to some lineages, which are not classified by TFClass) have all possible TFClass families separated by ';'. In validation tests with TFs of cow, dog, and opossum classified by TFClass, TFs assigned to a single family were assigned to the correct family in >99% of the cases.

In all schemes, classification levels without a more specific level are filled with the name of the more general level. For example, PlantTFDB family bHLH has no subfamilies, so its subfamily is bHLH.

The classification schemes are available in the data sets planttfdb_scheme (PlantTFDB), tapscan_scheme (TAPscan), planttfclass_scheme (correspondence between TAPscan and Plant-TFClass), cisbp_scheme (CIS-BP), and tfclass_scheme (correspondence between CIS-BP and TFClass).

References

Jin, J., Tian, F., Yang, D. C., Meng, Y. Q., Kong, L., Luo, J., & Gao, G. (2017). PlantTFDB 4.0: toward a central hub for transcription factors and regulatory interactions in plants. Nucleic Acids Research, 45(D1), D1040-D1045.

Petroll, R., Varshney, D., Hiltemann, S., Finke, H., Schreiber, M., de Vries, J., & Rensing, S. A. (2025). Enhanced sensitivity of TAPscan v4 enables comprehensive analysis of streptophyte transcription factor evolution. The Plant Journal, 121(1), e17184.

Blanc-Mathieu, R., Dumas, R., Turchi, L., Lucas, J., & Parcy, F. (2024). Plant-TFClass: a structural classification for plant transcription factors. Trends in Plant Science, 29(1), 40-51.

Weirauch, M. T., Yang, A., Albu, M., Cote, A. G., Montenegro-Montero, A., Drewe, P., ... & Hughes, T. R. (2014). Determination and inference of eukaryotic transcription factor sequence specificity. Cell, 158(6), 1431-1443.

Wingender, E., Schoeps, T., Haubrock, M., Krull, M., & Dönitz, J. (2018). TFClass: expanding the classification of human transcription factors to their mammalian orthologs. Nucleic Acids Research, 46(D1), D343-D347.

Examples

data(gsu_annotation)
families <- classify_tfs(gsu_annotation)
head(families)
#>         Gene     PlantTFDB_family PlantTFDB_subfamily TAPscan_family
#> 1 AIG92585.1                 <NA>                <NA>            HAT
#> 2 gsu04730.1             Nin-like            Nin-like         RWP-RK
#> 3 gsu05000.1             Nin-like            Nin-like         RWP-RK
#> 4 gsu06140.1 GARP;MYB superfamily G2-like;MYB-related            MYB
#> 5 gsu06730.1                 <NA>                <NA>           bZIP
#> 6 gsu07030.1                 <NA>                <NA>            PHD
#>   TAPscan_subfamily TAP_class  PlantTFClass_superclass
#> 1              GNAT        TR                     <NA>
#> 2               RKD        TF Helix-turn-helix domains
#> 3               RKD        TF Helix-turn-helix domains
#> 4       MYB-related        TF Helix-turn-helix domains
#> 5              bZIP        TF            Basic domains
#> 6               PHD        TR                     <NA>
#>                    PlantTFClass_class PlantTFClass_family CISBP_family
#> 1                                <NA>                <NA>         <NA>
#> 2                              RWP-RK              RWP-RK       RWP-RK
#> 3                              RWP-RK              RWP-RK       RWP-RK
#> 4          Tryptophan cluster factors         MYB-related     Myb/SANT
#> 5 Basic leucine zipper factors (bZIP)                bZIP         bZIP
#> 6                                <NA>                <NA>         <NA>
#>         TFClass_superclass                       TFClass_class
#> 1                     <NA>                                <NA>
#> 2                     <NA>                                <NA>
#> 3                     <NA>                                <NA>
#> 4 Helix-turn-helix domains          Tryptophan cluster factors
#> 5            Basic domains Basic leucine zipper factors (bZIP)
#> 6                     <NA>                                <NA>
#>                                                                                          TFClass_family
#> 1                                                                                                  <NA>
#> 2                                                                                                  <NA>
#> 3                                                                                                  <NA>
#> 4                                                                                              Myb-SANT
#> 5 Jun-related;Fos-related;Maf-related;B-ATF-related;XBP1-related;ATF4-related;CREB-related;CEBP-related
#> 6                                                                                                  <NA>

# Only TAPscan classifications, with TAP classes (TF, TR, or PT)
tapscan_families <- classify_tfs(gsu_annotation, scheme = "TAPscan")
table(tapscan_families$TAP_class)
#> 
#>  PT  TF  TR 
#>   9 143  96 

# Only CIS-BP classifications
cisbp_families <- classify_tfs(gsu_annotation, scheme = "CISBP")
head(cisbp_families)
#>          Gene CISBP_family
#> 1  gsu04730.1       RWP-RK
#> 2  gsu05000.1       RWP-RK
#> 3  gsu06140.1     Myb/SANT
#> 4  gsu06730.1         bZIP
#> 5  gsu08760.1           DM
#> 6 gsu100410.1       RWP-RK

# TFClass classifications (inferred from CIS-BP families)
tfclass_families <- classify_tfs(gsu_annotation, scheme = "TFClass")
head(tfclass_families)
